purpose: Diagnostic comparison of debug-console and native Windows release execution; not a physical validation or release-gate qualification.
method: Each runtime manually advanced the same 240 Hz Simulation.step() path for two counterbalanced rounds, with 120 warmup and 600 measured ticks per aircraft per round. Microprofile timings are independent evaluator measurements and are not additive.
host_observation: Parent confirmed the integration suite, platform exports/smokes, and endurance run had finished before this paired timing. Immediately after the release run and before the debug run, one long-running Godot process was observed: PID 88100, Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe with --path app --script research/flight-dynamics/climb-trim/watch.gd. It was left untouched. Per-run CPU load was not sampled, so host isolation is unqualified and the timings are diagnostic.

provenance_checks.main_pack: Embedded in the executable; the executable SHA-256 binds the exported artifact.

interpretation: The native release build is faster than the debug-console run for all three cases, but both glow families remain well above the 500 us median-p95 target.
The legacy release case is near the target: its median-of-round p95 is 504 us and its worst round is 516 us, so the run does not pass a 500 us gate.
The paired run is diagnostic only because host isolation was not controlled and a persistent climb-trim watcher was observed around the measurement window.
The 2T and 4T family timings should not be ranked as a physical superiority claim; these are candidate installations with estimated or inferred component properties.
limitations: Only two measurement rounds per case were taken.
No profiler was attached to the native release executable; stage microprofiles are separate sampled evaluator calls.
Candidate propeller inertia uses a uniform-box inventory surrogate and crank inertia is inferred (2e-5 kg m2 for 2T, 3e-5 kg m2 for 4T); no matched measurements exist.

postflight_repository_check.note: Both timed runs and the embedded release manifest bind the same source snapshot. A postflight check found app/sim/flight_session.gd differs in the current worktree due concurrent lake-context integration edits; the paired performance result describes the recorded snapshot and does not claim to measure those later edits. The input maps still match the current worktree.
